title: Quad-layout quantization stage: 1.5 s to under 100 ms
description: Make the `quantization` stage of QuadLayoutEngine fast. It takes 1.526 s today. The startup CPU profile shows ojAlgo DenseTableau (doPivot, doubleValue) high in self time, i.e. a dense LP/ILP. Related: PATCH-69, PATCH-90 (replace the ILP with metriko-style greedy basis-loop quantization). Baseline, measured 2026-10-15 with `uv run ixdar-cli run-scene --scene quad-layout --property quadLayoutScene.alpha=15` on the default model (headless, 9.1 s to ready): cross field 0.395 s, seamless 0.800 s, motorcycle graph 0.145 s, quantization 1.526 s, carve 0.674 s, contract 1.475 s, global grid map 1.897 s. These run synchronously before the scene's first frame, so together they are almost all of the quad-layout scene's time to first paint. The user's goal is first paint under 0.1 s; a sibling ticket moves the pipeline off the first frame, and each stage ticket makes one stage as fast as it can go. Target: this stage under 100 ms on the default model, or as close as the algorithm allows, with the reason it can go no lower. The stage's output must not change: same singularity count, arc/node/patch counts, quad count and a screenshot that image-diffs clean against the master baseline. Use the stage's own `[quad-layout] <stage>` log line and an async-profiler capture (`run-scene --profile`, read with `ixdar-cli profile-report`). Stay inside this stage's package; touch shared code (solver/, HalfEdgeMesh, QuadLayoutEngine) only where the stage needs it, and list every shared-file change in the report, because six sibling tickets run in parallel. Related: CRAW-2 (scan-scale pipeline), CRAW-4 (cached layouts).
definition-of-done:
1. The stage's `[quad-layout] quantization` time on the default quad-layout model is recorded before and after (median of 3 runs) in changes-made, with the after time under 100 ms or a stated reason it cannot be. 2. Singularity count, arc/node/patch counts and quad count match master exactly. 3. A screenshot of the final layout under tmp/ image-diffs clean against a master screenshot taken the same way. 4. No debugging scaffolding is left behind; `ixd wt done` passes.

5. Whole-suite check: `python3 /home/acw/Code/Ixdar/tmp/quad-suite/run_suite.py --checkout <this worktree> --out /home/acw/Code/Ixdar/tmp/quad-suite/<ticket> --compare /home/acw/Code/Ixdar/tmp/quad-suite/master-0f52d26f` covers sphere_base, sphere_random, bolt, hand, fandisk, elk, feline, fertility, botijo, block, Hand-tri-30k, rockerarm, buddha and the crawfish scan (~/crawfish/IMG_4109.glb, 8 GB heap). Every mesh reports MATCH against the master baseline: the same status (a mesh master fails on must fail the same way), the same count signature, and an identical screenshot. The per-mesh stage times before/after go in changes-made. A DIFF stops for a user ruling.
testing-plan: 1. On master: run-scene quad-layout three times, record the stage time and counts, take a screenshot. 2. In the worktree: the same three runs plus a profile capture; compare times and counts. 3. image-diff the two screenshots. 4. mvn test for the touched packages.
unknowns: Whether the stage can reach 100 ms without changing its output; if not, what the floor is and why
changes-made: Relaunch checkpoint (agent 2): previous agent replaced the ojAlgo ILP with a self-contained IntegerProgram (cover-dominance + unimodular-substitution presolve, bounded dual simplex, best-first branch and bound) and reused the final ZeroArcCollapse in LayoutExtraction (dropped the unread layoutRecordsByFace buffer). ojAlgo removed from ixdar-app/pom.xml and the Platform.newIntegerProgram hook removed from Platform, HeadlessPlatform, LwjglPlatform, WebPlatform; git grep shows no other ojAlgo user in the repo or in the CRAW-72/ENG-14 worktrees. Master baseline (3 runs, loaded machine): quantization 1.916/2.344/2.624 s, median 2.344 s (ticket's earlier 1.526 s). Interim runs of the new solver: 0.086-0.186 s, identical counts (singularities 72, arcs 6792, nodes 3468, patches 3316, objective 4172.578, zeroArcs 4493, clusters 371, quads 14444).

Result: [quad-layout] quantization median of 3 on the default model: master 1.585 s (1.664/1.585/1.574, main checkout) -> 0.046 s (0.054/0.046/0.039, worktree). Counts identical to master: singularities 72, arcs 6792, nodes 3468, patches 3316, objective 4172.578, zeroArcs 4493/6792, clusters 371 (72 singular), skeletonArcs 2299, tJunctions 6, recarve nodes 446 arcs 908 patches 454, quads 14444. tmp/craw-69-after-1.png vs tmp/craw-69-master-1.png: image-diff rmse 0, 0 differing pixels (identical sha256). ojAlgo is no longer a dependency (no other user in the repo). TEMP timing lines removed; LayoutExtraction keeps master's countOpenFeatureEdges shape. Added unit.mesh.IntegerProgramTest (fractional relaxation closed by branching with a substituted variable, presolve infeasibility, negative-weight rejection); it and the collapse fixture tests pass.

Whole-suite check (fixed runner, worktree code, vs master 0f52d26f): 13 of 14 MATCH (identical counts and screenshots; quantization e.g. botijo/block/rockerarm/buddha 1.5/0.75/0.19/0.34 s -> 0.06/0.03/0.01/0.05 s). DIFF on sphere_random: master and branch reach the same OPTIMAL objective 550.017 in separation round 1 but pick different optima among ties (zeroArcs 1091 on master vs 1087), so the runs diverge; master later fails with 'degenerate chart', the branch dies with java.lang.OutOfMemoryError (default heap). sphere_random, fandisk, Hand-tri-30k and the crawfish fail to load on master, so they do not exercise the pipeline. Waiting on a user ruling about tie-breaking.

Tie-break progress (agent 3): user ruled for a deterministic tie-break. IntegerProgram now returns, among assignments within a relative 1e-9 of the optimum, the one with most zero variables, then the lexicographically smallest vector (Lyon 2021 §5 states no preference among optima). It runs only when branch and bound cannot rule out a second optimum (a node pruned within the tolerance, or a free nonbasic with ~0 reduced cost at the optimal node): a best-first count search over indicator columns, then a depth-first lexicographic search, both in the presolved columns with an objective-ceiling row; no epsilon weighting, so the primary optimum is untouched. Two unit tests added (ties decided by count and by lex; a 1e-6 near-tie must keep the cheaper, less sparse optimum); IntegerProgramTest 5/5 green. Next: stage timings and the suite.

Tie-break finished (agent 4): compiles, IntegerProgramTest 5/5 green, TEMP diagnostics stripped. Probe before stripping: on botijo and buddha the tie-break never fires (branch and bound proves a unique optimum). On sphere_random it fires every separation round, 3-18 ms each; round 0 has the same objective 545.653 and zeroArcs 1124 as master but a different solution (52 presolved columns changed, master merges 5 clusters there, the branch 8), so the runs diverge from round 0. Lyon 2021 s5 states no preference among optima; s4.3 motivates the objective as promoting coarseness, which most-zeros follows.

Tie-break cost fix (agent 4): on sphere_random the tie-break's count search grew to 46 s per separation round (500k nodes on one 69-column component), quantization 698 s in total. Cause: the indicator row x - U*y used U = ceiling/weight, so the count relaxation was near zero. Added bound propagation over each component's rows and U from x's propagated maximum. Same 50 per-round ILP results (objective, zeroArcs) as before, quantization 698 s -> 61.7 s; master's is 3.5 s over 42 rounds before it fails with 'degenerate chart', which the branch also does. IntegerProgramTest 5/5.

Quantization time, botijo and buddha (tie-break does not fire on either; branch and bound proves a unique optimum): before the tie-break 0.057 s / 0.054 s (single suite run); after, median of 3: botijo 0.049 s (0.049/0.033/0.059), buddha 0.040 s (0.073/0.035/0.040). No measurable change. Master: 0.342 s / 1.500 s.

Correction to the timing note: master quantization is botijo 1.500 s, buddha 0.342 s. Whole suite with the tie-break (vs master 0f52d26f): 13 of 14 MATCH (status, count signature, screenshot). Quantization master -> branch: sphere_base 0.150->0.005, bolt 0.191->0.005, hand 0.262->0.038, fandisk 0.225->0.030, elk 0.934->0.030, feline 3.909->0.236, fertility 0.336->0.023, botijo 1.500->0.033, block 0.753->0.081, Hand-tri-30k 0.220->0.016, rockerarm 0.187->0.009, buddha 0.342->0.040, sphere_random 3.524->71.3 s. fandisk, Hand-tri-30k, crawfish and sphere_random fail to load on master and fail the same way here. RE-BASELINED sphere_random (tied optima): separation round 0 has the same objective 545.653 and zeroArcs 1124/1621 on master and branch but a different solution (master merges 5 clusters and adds 39 cuts, the branch 8 and 43), so later rounds solve different programs (round 1: master 550.017/1091, branch 549.318/1099). New counts: 50 separation rounds, final round 49 objective 550.017 zeroArcs 1062/1621; outcome load-failed with the same error as master, 'source active face 456 has a degenerate chart' (no OutOfMemoryError now). Open cost: sphere_random's quantization is 71 s against master's 3.5 s, almost all of it the tie-break's exact sparsest-solution search on a 69-column component in later rounds (~1 s per round after the propagation fix, 46 s before).
